findings.description: AWS access key ID and secret access key are hard-coded in plaintext within the EC2 user_data script, exposing long-lived IAM credentials to anyone with access to instance metadata, the Terraform state, or console/API describe-instance-attribute calls.
Ingress rule allows SSH (port 22) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing the management plane of the instance to the entire internet and enabling brute-force or credential-stuffing attacks.
Ingress rule allows HTTP (port 80) from 0.0.0.0/0 with no TLS, meaning any traffic to the web server, including credentials or session data, is transmitted and reachable in cleartext from any source.
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, automatically assigning public IPs to any instance launched in this subnet, increasing the internet-facing attack surface.
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, automatically assigning public IPs to any instance launched in this subnet, increasing the internet-facing attack surface.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true, so data stored on the volume attached to the portal server is unencrypted at rest.
The S3 bucket used to store VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration, leaving potentially sensitive network traffic metadata unencrypted at rest.

findings.issue_category: missing access controls / public access block
findings.description: The bucket has no public access block or bucket policy restricting access, and force_destroy is enabled, so there is no defense-in-depth control preventing accidental public exposure of flow log data.
